title: Titanium Femoral Condyle
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-7Nb (ASTM F1295) is a vanadium-free medical alloy using niobium as the beta stabilizer, eliminating concerns about vanadium toxicity while maintaining mechanical properties comparable to Ti-6Al-4V.
commonFailures: Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86)
Thread damage from improper installation torque exceeding recommended values
Galvanic corrosion at interface with dissimilar metals in electrolyte environments

faq.q: What is a titanium femoral condyle?
faq.a: A titanium femoral condyle is a precision-machined orthopedic joints component used in total knee femoral condyle component (ti-6al-7nb). Manufactured from Ti-6Al-7Nb (ASTM F1295) for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What is the typical application for titanium femoral condyle?
faq.a: Titanium Femoral Condyle is designed for total knee femoral condyle component (ti-6al-7nb). The Ti-6Al-7Nb (ASTM F1295) grade is selected to provide the optimal balance of strength, fatigue life, and environmental resistance for this specific application.

faq.q: How is titanium femoral condyle manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Femoral Condyle is manufactured using VAR melting. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium femoral condyle?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
